mainTopic: Mourner's conduct: the house of mourning, the weekly return to normal life, marriage and pressed clothes during the שלשים, and how שבת counts in mourning
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a mourner. Seven people read from the Torah and then leave, and רבי יהושע בן קרחה adds that they should sit and mourn quietly rather than stroll in the market. People do not discuss שמועה or אגדה in a house of mourning, though רבי חנניה בן גמליאל was known to do so. A ברייתא then lays out how a mourner returns to public life step by step over four weeks. רבי יהודה shifts every stage one week later, making five weeks. Next come rules for the שלשים. No one marries during the thirty days. A widower must wait three רגלים, or two according to רבי יהודה, unless he has no children or has young children who need care. The story of יוסף הכהן shows the young-children exception, and רב פפא explains that he waited thirty days before living with his new wife. Three תנאים disagree about which pressed clothes are forbidden, and אביי and רבא each dressed according to a different view. Finally, the גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that שבת counts toward the mourning days but does not interrupt them. It begins describing how יהודה and the גליל differed in practice, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Seven read from the Torah, then they leave
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier ברייתא: seven people read from the Torah, and then they leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And seven people read from the Torah, and then they leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that started before this section. It describes a Torah reading of seven people in the mourning setting, after which everyone leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes out a description that is already in progress. It sets up the next step, where רבי יהושע בן קרחה explains what 'they leave' does and does not mean.

phrases.english: And seven read from the Torah, and they leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹרִין שִׁבְעָה, וְיוֹצְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא already in progress
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven read from the Torah, and afterward the people leave.

steps.title: Leaving does not mean strolling in the market
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה clarifies that after leaving, people should not wander the market but should sit and mourn quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: They should not go and stroll in the marketplace. Instead, they sit and mourn quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן קרחה explains the word 'they leave' from the previous step. It does not allow people to go out and walk around freely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 could sound like people are free once they leave. רבי יהושע בן קרחה limits that: the mood of mourning continues, so they sit at home in silent grief and do not go strolling in public.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Not that they go and stroll in the marketplace,
rather they sit and mourn quietly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the meaning of 'they leave' from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After leaving, they do not stroll in the market; they sit and mourn.

steps.title: No Torah teaching in a house of mourning
steps.stepSummary: People do not speak about שמועה or אגדה in a house of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people do not say halachic teachings or אגדה in a house of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another rule: Torah discussion, both halachic and אגדה, is not held in a house of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning Torah brings joy, and that does not fit the mood of the mourner's home. So even this מצוה-type activity is held back there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that even Torah study is limited during mourning because it brings happiness.

phrases.english: And they do not say halachic teachings or אגדה
in a house of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים שְׁמוּעָה וְאַגָּדָה בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another rule about conduct in the mourning setting
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No שמועה or אגדה is said in a house of mourning.

steps.title: רבי חנניה בן גמליאל did teach there
steps.stepSummary: A report that רבי חנניה בן גמליאל would say שמועה and אגדה in a house of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי חנניה בן גמליאל that he would say halachic teachings and אגדה in a house of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the rule in step 3, the text reports one sage who acted differently and did teach Torah in a house of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows a contrasting practice next to the general rule. The text does not explain why he did it; it only records that he did.

keyTerms.meaning: they said about him (a report of someone's practice)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר שְׁמוּעָה וְאַגָּדָה בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל.
phrases.english: that he would say halachic teachings and אגדה in a house of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records a practice that contrasts with the rule in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנניה בן גמליאל used to teach שמועה and אגדה in a house of mourning.

steps.title: Four weeks of returning to normal life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the mourner's stages: week 1 he stays home, week 2 he goes out but not to his usual seat, week 3 he sits in his seat but does not speak, week 4 he is like everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A mourner, in the first week, does not go out of the door of his house. In the second week, he goes out but does not sit in his usual place. In the third week, he sits in his usual place but does not speak. In the fourth week, he is like any other person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that describes how a mourner slowly returns to public life, one stage per week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each week removes one restriction. First he does not leave home. Then he may go out, but not to his regular seat in shul. Then he may take his seat, but stays silent. By the fourth week all these limits are gone.

keyTerms.meaning: in his usual place (his regular seat in shul)

steps.confusionAlert: Here שַׁבָּת means a week, not the day of שבת. 'שַׁבָּת רִאשׁוֹנָה' is the first week of mourning.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A mourner, in the first week,
does not go out of the door of his house;
in the second week, he goes out
but does not sit in his usual place;
phrases.notes: His usual place means his regular seat in shul.

phrases.english: in the third week, he sits in his usual place
but does not speak;
in the fourth week, he is like any other person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָבֵל, שַׁבָּת רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the mourner's weekly stages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four stages over four weeks: stay home, go out but not to his seat, sit but not speak, then fully normal.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the first-week rule is obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says there was no need to say a mourner stays home in the first week, because everyone comes to his house to comfort him anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They did not need to say that in the first week he does not go out of the door of his house, because everyone comes into his house to comfort him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes back on the first stage of the ברייתא in step 5. He says that stage teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first week, everyone is coming to the mourner's home to comfort him, so of course he is home. A rule telling him to stay home adds nothing. This sets up his own corrected list in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: they did not need to say it (it is obvious)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They did not need to say

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת רִאשׁוֹנָה לֹא יֵצֵא מִפֶּתַח בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: that in the first week he may not go out of the door of his house,
since everyone comes into his house to comfort him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first stage of the ברייתא in step 5 as unnecessary
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the first-week stage of the תנא קמא's list
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule is obvious, since in the first week everyone comes to his house to comfort him.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's five-week schedule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה moves each stage one week later: week 2 stay home, week 3 go out but not to his seat, week 4 sit but not speak, week 5 like everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in the second week he does not go out of the door of his house. In the third week he goes out but does not sit in his usual place. In the fourth week he sits in his usual place but does not speak. In the fifth week he is like any other person.
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the first-week rule is pointless, רבי יהודה gives his own list. Every stage starts one week later than in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the stages is the same as in step 5; only the timing changes. Staying home becomes a real rule for the second week, when visitors stop coming. So the mourner returns to normal only in the fifth week instead of the fourth.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: four weeks (home, out but not his seat, his seat but silent, normal). רבי יהודה: the first week is obvious, so the same stages shift one week later and he is normal only in the fifth week.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: שְׁנִיָּה — אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִפֶּתַח בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Rather: in the second week, he does not go out of the door of his house;
in the third week, he goes out but does not sit in his usual place;
in the fourth week, he sits in his usual place but does not speak;
in the fifth week, he is like any other person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שְׁנִיָּה — אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִפֶּתַח בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's replacement schedule after his objection in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each stage moves one week later; the mourner is like everyone else only in the fifth week.

steps.title: No marrying during the thirty days, and a widower waits three Festivals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids marriage during the שלשים, and a widower may not remarry until three רגלים have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: During all thirty days, marrying is forbidden. If a man's wife died, he may not marry another woman until three Festivals have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with two marriage rules for mourners. The first is general, and the second is a longer wait for a man whose wife died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any mourner may not marry during the שלשים. A widower has a much longer wait: he may not remarry until three רגלים have passed since his wife died.

keyTerms.meaning: The three pilgrimage Festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
All thirty days apply to marrying.
phrases.notes: He means that during the thirty days of mourning, a mourner may not get married.

phrases.english: If his wife died,
it is forbidden to marry another woman
until three Festivals pass over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לַנִּישּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mourner's weekly stages to a new topic: marriage during mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No marriage during the שלשים. A widower may not remarry until three רגלים pass.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: two Festivals are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the widower only waits through two רגלים; before the third he may already marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: During the first and second Festivals it is forbidden; by the third, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and shortens the widower's waiting time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion requires three full רגלים to pass. רבי יהודה says that once two have passed, the man may marry even before the third arrives. The disagreement is only about how long he waits; both agree that he must wait.

keyTerms.meaning: A Festival (one of the three רגלים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the first and second Festival: forbidden;
the third: permitted.
phrases.notes: He means that once two Festivals have passed, he may marry before the third one comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רֶגֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the three-רגלים waiting period in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widower waits through two רגלים and may marry before the third.

steps.title: Exceptions: no children, or young children
steps.stepSummary: A widower with no children, or with young children, may remarry right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has no children, he may marry immediately, so he does not hold back from the מצוה of having children. If she left him young children, he may marry immediately so that someone will care for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives two cases where the widower does not have to wait at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first exception protects the מצוה of פריה ורביה, which he has not yet fulfilled. The second protects his young children, who need someone to take care of them. In both cases, a pressing need overrides the waiting period.
steps.whatToRemember: The widower's waiting period gives way when he has no children yet, or when he has small children who need care.

phrases.english: And if he has no children,
he is permitted to marry immediately
because of neglecting being fruitful and multiplying.
If she left him young children,
he is permitted to marry immediately
because of their care.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ בָּנִים — מוּתָּר לִישָּׂא לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives exceptions to the widower's waiting period from steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widower with no children, or with young children, may remarry immediately.

steps.title: The story of יוסף הכהן
steps.stepSummary: יוסף הכהן arranged right away at the cemetery to marry his late wife's sister so she could raise his children, but he waited a long time before living with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case where the wife of יוסף הכהן died. At the cemetery he said to her sister, 'Go and take care of your sister's children.' Even so, he did not live with her until a long time later.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a real-life story that shows the young-children exception being put into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף הכהן married immediately because his children needed care, just as the exception allows. However, he held back from living with her as husband and wife. This shows that the exception permits the marriage itself, but some delay still applies to the relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident brought as an example
Lived with her as husband and wife

phrases.english: There was an incident where the wife died
of Yosef the Kohen,
and he said to her sister at the cemetery:
Go and take care of your sister's children.
phrases.notes: This was his way of asking her to marry him right away.

phrases.english: And even so,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ אֶלָּא לִזְמַן מְרוּבֶּה.
phrases.english: he did not live with her until a long time later.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמֵּתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the young-children exception from step 10 in a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a widower with young children may marry immediately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of יוסף הכהן, who married his wife's sister right away but waited to live with her.

steps.title: How long is a long time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story means by 'a long time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'a long time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to clarify a vague phrase in the story. It is setting up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A long time' does not tell us an actual length of time. The גמרא wants a concrete number so the practical rule is clear.

phrases.english: What is "a long time"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לִזְמַן מְרוּבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase from the story in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of time meant by 'a long time.'

steps.title: רב פפא: after thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'a long time' means after the שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: After thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: he waited until the thirty days of mourning were over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So even when the marriage is allowed right away, living together waits until the שלשים has passed. This connects back to the opening rule that the thirty days are a time with no marriage.
steps.whatToRemember: A widower with young children may marry at once, but he waits until after the שלשים to live with his new wife.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
After thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'A long time' means after thirty days.

steps.title: No freshly pressed clothes during the thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids a mourner from wearing pressed clothes during the שלשים, whether the clothes are new or old.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: During all thirty days, ironed clothes are forbidden, whether they are new garments or old garments coming out of the press.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about another restriction: wearing freshly pressed clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this first opinion, the rule includes even old clothes. If they just came out of the press, they are forbidden too, because freshly pressed clothes look new and fancy.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
All thirty days apply to ironed clothes,
whether new garments
or old garments
coming out of the press.
phrases.notes: These are clothes fresh from pressing, which look like new.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם לְגִיהוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from marriage to a new שלשים restriction: pressed clothes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the שלשים, all freshly pressed garments, new or old, are forbidden.

steps.title: רבי: only new garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי limits the rule to new garments only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: They forbade only new garments.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with the first opinion and narrows the restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, old clothes that were pressed are allowed. Only new garments are forbidden during the שלשים.

phrases.english: Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: They forbade only new garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only new garments are forbidden during the שלשים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: only new white garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון narrows the rule even more, to new white garments only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: They forbade only new white garments.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion limits the restriction further than רבי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the forbidden category shrinks a third time. Now only clothes that are both new and white are forbidden; new colored clothes are allowed. Each opinion narrows the rule a step more than the one before it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on pressed clothes: all freshly pressed garments, only new ones, or only new white ones.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים לְבָנִים בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: They forbade only new white garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים לְבָנִים בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי's view from step 15 even further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only new white garments are forbidden during the שלשים.

steps.title: אביי wears an old white garment
steps.stepSummary: אביי, while in mourning, went out in an old white garment, following רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי went out in an old white garment, following רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how אביי dressed while he was in mourning. He followed the opinion of רבי from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the ban on pressed clothes during the שלשים covers only new garments. So an old garment, even a white one, is allowed. אביי wore an old white garment, which shows he ruled like רבי.

phrases.english: Abaye went out (while in mourning)
in an old white garment, following Rabbi.
phrases.notes: Back in Step 15, רבי said only new garments are forbidden. So an old one is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי נָפֵיק בִּגְרָדָא דְסַרְבָּלָא כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows an אמורא's practice that follows רבי's view from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי ruled like רבי: an old garment may be worn during the שלשים.

steps.title: רבא wears a new red Roman cloak
steps.stepSummary: רבא, while in mourning, went out in a new red Roman cloak, following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא went out in a new red Roman cloak, following רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רבא dressed differently from אביי. He followed the opinion of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון forbade only new white garments. A new garment that is red is not white, so it is allowed. That is why רבא could wear a brand-new red cloak.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי followed רבי, so old garments are allowed. רבא followed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so even new garments are allowed as long as they are not white.

phrases.english: Rava went out in a Roman cloak
a red, new one,
following Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: In Step 16 he forbade only new white clothes. Red isn't white, so it's allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא נָפֵיק בְּחִימּוּצְתָּא רוֹמִיתָא סוּמַּקְתָּא חַדְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with אביי's practice by showing an אמורא who followed the most lenient view from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא ruled like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: only new white garments are forbidden during the שלשים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: שבת counts but does not interrupt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה: שבת counts toward the days of mourning but does not interrupt them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they said: שבת counts and does not interrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This line will be explained in the steps that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two parts. 'עולה' means שבת counts as one of the seven days of mourning. 'אינה מפסקת' means שבת does not end or break the mourning; it continues after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת counts toward the mourning days
and it does not interrupt the mourning

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with a יום טוב. Here the point is that שבת counts as a mourning day, yet the mourning still goes on after it.

phrases.english: Because they said:
Shabbat counts and does not interrupt.
phrases.notes: 'Counts' means it is one of the seven days. 'Does not interrupt' means the mourning keeps going after שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: שַׁבָּת עוֹלָה וְאֵינָהּ מַפְסֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of clothing during the שלשים and opens discussion of a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת counts as one of the mourning days, but the mourning continues after it.

steps.title: Judea and the Galilee practiced differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a teaching about how the people of יהודה and the people of the גליל differed in practice, starting with what one group says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of יהודה and the people of the גליל: these say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It introduces two groups, the people of יהודה and the people of the גליל, and starts to tell us what the first group says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line opens a comparison between two regions about mourning on שבת. The actual positions come right after 'הני אמרי'. For now, the learner just needs to know that two different customs are about to be described.

phrases.english: The people of Judea and the people of the Galilee.
These say:

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה וּבְנֵי גָלִילָא. הָנֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the משנה's rule about שבת and mourning by introducing two regional customs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a difference in practice between יהודה and the גליל about mourning on שבת (details follow).
